leading_positions.synthesis: Four members include B002 (collateral constraints and credit cycles) in their round 1 preferred configuration. Boppart, Krusell and Teorell prefer Kiyotaki and Moore alone. Hassler, the chair, is the only member whose preferred part adds Gertler, and he accepts the two-name version as a fallback. Krusell and Teorell dropped Gertler after reading colleagues' openings. Teorell lists B002 with Gertler as a single-part fallback if the Committee rejects Pakes-alone for B012. All four cite the originality of the mechanism, nearly three decades of use and the clean origin of the 1997 paper. All four also flag overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises, and weaker empirical identification of the size of the amplification. Teorell pairs B002 with a second part, B012, so his configuration differs from the other three. This is not a six-vote position on its own.

Four members include B012 (structural demand and industry estimation) in their preferred configuration, but they do not propose the same laureates. Andersson, Hjalmarsson and Stromberg prefer Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn as the sole part. Teorell would credit Pakes alone as a second part alongside B002, and he records the omission of Berry and Levinsohn as a real attribution loss. The shared case is the reach of the method (merger review, antitrust, trade, health), about thirty years of replication and critique, and a compact BLP core. The shared reservations are the omission of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, the weight given to a method relative to a substantive discovery, and the dependence on structural assumptions. Friberg, Hassler and Krusell name B012 only as an alternative, so their support for it is weaker than the four counted here.

Dreber and Friberg prefer B025 (firm heterogeneity and trade) with Helpman and Melitz, and both exclude Redding for cleaner attribution. They argue that Melitz-style selection is distinct from Krugman's 2008 prize and has more than twenty years of firm-level confirmation. Both concede that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited, so the attribution is incomplete, and both treat B002 as a serious alternative. Seven others name B025 as an alternative (Boppart, Enflo, Fredriksson, Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Krusell, Stromberg), but only these two prefer it as the main part. Krusell is skeptical about how distinct it is from Krugman's prize, and Teorell ranked it eighth at opening and names it neither as a preferred part nor as an alternative.

Only Teorell proposes a two-part configuration: Kiyotaki and Moore for B002, and Pakes alone for B012. He uses the three-person cap as a reason to drop Gertler and to credit one name for B012. He acknowledges that a prize pairing macro-finance with empirical IO has no obvious shared theme, and that Pakes-alone omits Berry and Levinsohn from BLP. No other member's preferred configuration combines these ballots. Friberg, Hassler and Krusell treat B002 and B012 or B025 as alternatives rather than as combined parts.

Fredriksson alone prefers B050 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) as the main part. He describes it as a coherent programme joining formal theory and testable implications about electoral rules, state capacity and fiscal policy. He concedes that the cross-country identification is thinner than the theory's influence, that the 2024 institutions prize is adjacent, and that it is the narrowest-supported shortlisted candidate. Teorell lists B050 as an alternative, and Krusell and Hassler are not recorded as supporting it in round 1. Besley's inclusion is the most debatable part of the attribution.

Enflo alone prefers B021 (trade shocks and technology in labour markets), confined to Autor, Hanson and Dorn and to the trade-shock core. Her case rests on a decade of replication and contestation with new local-labour-market data. Boppart (second at opening) and Dreber (sixth) concede that the evidence is strong but say the bundling of tasks and trade shocks, the task-framework originators outside the credited names, and the unsettled persistence and shift-share debates keep it as an alternative or out of their ordering. Fredriksson would credit Autor and Hanson only.

areas_of_agreement: All eleven files name B002 as either a preferred part (Boppart, Hassler, Krusell, Teorell) or an alternative (the other seven). No file argues against the Kiyotaki-Moore 1997 mechanism as a mature, conceptually original contribution with clean two-author credit.

Nine of the other ten files either prefer Kiyotaki and Moore alone or explicitly decline to add Gertler (Andersson, Boppart, Dreber, Enflo, Fredriksson, Friberg, Hjalmarsson, Krusell, Teorell). Their reasons are the Bernanke lineage of the accelerator, the 2022 overlap, and Gertler's divided credit with B043. Hassler is the only member who prefers a three-name B002 part, and he accepts two names as a fallback.

B002, B012 and B025 are the three candidates named in preferred configurations by nine of eleven members (including Teorell's two parts). Fifteen of the twenty-two alternatives listed in the files are B002, B012 or B025 (B002 six, B025 seven, B012 three, plus the preferred-part appearances noted above). The remaining preferred or alternative picks are B021, B050 and B001.

Members apply similar criteria: originality of the mechanism or method, breadth of downstream use, years of confirmation, and clarity of credit. Several explicitly say that the number of first-place votes at opening is not evidence of merit.

Maturity is not contested for B002, B012, B025 or B050, whose core work is described as about 20 to 30 years old. Several members explicitly discount their own field affinity when assessing candidates.
scientific_disputes: Mechanism or method: Hjalmarsson, Andersson and Stromberg treat BLP and dynamic-industry estimation as a framework with identifiable economic content (markups, substitution, welfare). Boppart, Friberg and Krusell are wary of letting a method's wide use stand in for a discovery. The weight given to conceptual mechanism relative to measurement tools remains unresolved.

Empirical identification of collateral amplification in B002: Boppart, Dreber, Enflo, Fredriksson, Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Krusell, Stromberg and Teorell all note that identification of the magnitude is weaker than the theory's influence. They differ on how much this should count against it.

Whether the 2022 prize on banks, runs and financial crises covers the collateral-constraint mechanism. Boppart argues the mechanisms are distinct, Teorell is uncertain it covers the accelerator, and Hassler separates Gertler's later intermediary-based work from the 2022 recognition. Krusell, Andersson and Enflo treat the overlap as a real risk.

B025: the size of gains from trade that depend specifically on the firm-heterogeneity channel, the sensitivity of Pareto-based results to functional form, and whether Krugman's 2008 prize leaves room are all debated.

B012: identification and computational critiques of structural estimation, and its dependence on functional-form and equilibrium assumptions, are recorded as active. Stromberg treats three decades of use through these debates as a sign of maturity.
B050: cross-country constitutional results face reverse-causality concerns, compared with the state-capacity and fiscal-capacity strand, as raised by Fredriksson, Teorell and Krusell.
B021: the long-run size of the China-shock effects and shift-share identification are contested. Enflo reads the debate as one over magnitudes, while Boppart and Dreber see an unsettled verdict.
attribution_disputes: B002 laureate set: Kiyotaki and Moore (Boppart, Krusell, Teorell as preferred; accepted by most others) versus Kiyotaki, Moore and Gertler (Hassler as preferred, with Teorell's conditional fallback). The proposals differ in laureates and therefore in citation scope. Hassler's three-name version also credits the broader finding that financial frictions propagate fluctuations, while the two-name version is a narrower collateral-and-credit-cycle citation. Gilchrist is treated as outside the core by Hassler and Andersson.

B012 laureate set: Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn (Andersson, Hjalmarsson, Stromberg) versus Pakes alone (Teorell). The Committee would also have to decide whether the omission of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin undermines a three-name citation. Hjalmarsson notes that if Bresnahan were judged equal in kind, no three-person set around BLP would be fully defensible.

B025: Helpman and Melitz are the preferred pair, but Dreber, Friberg, Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson, Krusell and Stromberg all record the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as an attribution gap. Redding is excluded by both supporters, and Hassler calls him later and more derivative.

B021: Enflo's trio (Autor, Hanson, Dorn) versus Fredriksson's Autor and Hanson only. Katz's credit overlaps with the skill-premium literature recognised in 2023, and Acemoglu and Restrepo are cited as task-framework originators outside the credited names.
B050: whether Besley should be included with Persson and Tabellini. Fredriksson concedes it is the more debatable inclusion.

Gertler's credit is divided between B002 and the eight-name B043. Several members treat this as a reason for a bounded citation, while Hassler treats it as a question of where his contribution is best placed.

Single-prize configuration constraint: Teorell's two-part proposal stays within the three-person cap only by dropping Gertler, Berry and Levinsohn. Dreber and Friberg note that other pairings would require dropping a name.
maturity_disputes: B021 is the only preferred candidate where maturity is explicitly contested. Enflo says about a decade of re-examination is enough, while Teorell (as quoted by Enflo) and Boppart consider the long-run verdict pending.

Adjacency to recent prizes is described variously as a timing and balance matter and as a merit matter: 2022 for B002, 2008 for B025, 2024 for B050 and B021. Members differ on whether adjacency is duplication or complementarity, and the files do not settle this.
No member disputes the maturity of the 1997 Kiyotaki-Moore paper, of BLP (1994 and 1995) or of Melitz (2003).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair (Hassler) is an explicit B002 supporter and the only member whose preferred part includes Gertler. His profile records frequent co-authorship and IIES colleagueship with Krusell and Boppart, who also prefer B002, and a 2026 co-authored paper with Friberg. None of these people is a candidate, and the files treat these as disclosures only. The chair also discloses topical affinity with B050 and B015, neither of which is in his preferred configuration.

Boppart discloses frequent co-authorship with Krusell and Hassler (both B002 supporters) and a long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow, a credited name on B017, which is in neither his preferred configuration nor his alternatives. He also notes weak evidence that he may have helped draft the 2025 Scientific Background, which does not bear on this slate.
Krusell discloses long-term co-authorship with Hassler and Boppart. None of the B002 credited names is among his listed co-authors.

Friberg discloses field adjacency to B025 and B012 and the 2026 paper with Hassler and Ellingsen. His spouse (Magdalena Andersson) is noted as a public fact with no apparent bearing on the candidates, and it is not treated as a conflict by him.

Teorell reports past co-authorship with Torsten Persson (B050, an alternative only) in his round 1 responses, but his own conflict note says the profile does not support identifying the co-author 'Persson' as Torsten Persson, so this is unverified. Fredriksson's file treats the disclosure as real without adjudicating it.
Enflo discloses collaboration with political scientists, including Johannes Lindvall, and that Teorell was formerly at Lund. Both relate to B050, not to her preferred part or alternatives.

Andersson notes field adjacency to B012 (matching, auctions, market design) without a personal connection. Dreber, Hjalmarsson and Stromberg report no candidate-specific connection. These flags are disclosed without adjudication, matching the protocol.
questions_for_round2: B002 citation scope: do members who prefer Kiyotaki and Moore alone regard the three-name version (with Gertler) as defensible if the citation is written around financial frictions in propagation, or do they oppose it in any form? What specific evidence separates Gertler's intermediary-based quantitative work from the 2022 recognition?

Mechanism versus method: if the Committee must choose between B002 (collateral constraints) and B012 (structural demand estimation) as a single part, which criterion should decide, and how would each side weigh B002's weaker empirical identification against B012's structural assumptions?

Teorell's two-part proposal: would members who prefer B002 or B012 alone accept a combined B002 (Kiyotaki, Moore) and B012 (Pakes) configuration? If not, is the objection thematic, attributional (Pakes alone omits Berry and Levinsohn), or both?

B012 attribution: would Andersson, Hjalmarsson and Stromberg support Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn if the citation were worded narrowly enough to avoid implying credit for all of empirical IO? What would change their view about Bresnahan, Benkard and Levin?

B025: how should the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and the Krugman 2008 overlap, weigh against a Helpman and Melitz pair? Do Dreber and Friberg hold B025 above B002 once these are weighed?
No position has six explicit preferred supporters. Which members whose first choice is B021, B025 or B050 would support B002 or B012 as their fallback, and on what citation? Which would not?

Prize overlap: should adjacency to the 2008, 2022 and 2024 prizes be treated as a merit criterion, a timing and balance criterion, or neither? Members are asked to state the principle they apply and to apply it to B002, B025, B050 and B021 consistently.
Evidence request: what in the record would members accept as evidence for the quantitative importance of collateral-driven amplification, and does any member change a ranking on that basis?
summary.chair_observation: No configuration reaches the six-vote majority on explicit round 1 preferences. B002 and B012 each have four explicit supporters. Teorell counts toward both and is the only member with a two-part configuration. B025 has two, and B050 and B021 one each. The chair is an explicit B002 supporter with the only three-name version, and this summary tries to give the opposing B012, B025, B050 and B021 arguments their full weight. The strongest shared ground is the Kiyotaki-Moore core, while the principal open questions are Gertler's inclusion, whether methods and mechanisms are weighed equally, the attribution gaps in B012 and B025, and the treatment of recent-prize overlap. This summary counts only positions explicit in the round 1 files and infers no hidden votes.
